text:
incident-bot: PAGE: P1 - elevated packet loss detected on IB fabric (rack-7). Service: inference-serving-prod. Symptoms: retransmit spikes -> container restarts, CUDA OOMs. Link: https://internal/redwood/incidents/2958123456

maria.lee: oncall Maria here, looking. Seeing cluster-wide QP retransmit bursts since ~12:02Z. Starting triage.

ajay.patel: attaching quick counters from node nd-7b: 
```
tx_retrans=1287 rx_retrans=1342 tx_drops=412 rx_drops=398 qps_in_err=4
link_state=flapping
```

ajay.patel: also seeing increased IB RNR NAKs. Could be a microburst causing HW queues to overwhelm.

sam.kim: confirming runtime logs show container restarts + CUDA OOMs on several shards. Example from runtime logs: 
```
2026-03-15T12:03:12Z [serve-3945] ERROR: CUDA out of memory on device 1 while allocating KV cache
2026-03-15T12:03:13Z [serve-3945] INFO: container restart (exit code 137)
2026-03-15T12:03:15Z [serve-4012] WARN: grpc stream reset, peer reset connection
```

jenna.hsu: customer impact telemetry: 3.5% of inference requests now 5xx (timeouts/restarts) across prod-us-east. Two Dedicated customers showing sustained latency spikes and error increase.

derek: quick mitigation proposal: 1) reduce per-request batch size and concurrency on affected pools 2) enable model-fallback to smaller quantized variant (cpu fallback if needed) 3) reduce K/V cross-node sharing to avoid extra RDMA chatter.

maria.lee: doing 1 & 3 now. Pushing a config to route the busy routes to local-kvcache-only and lowering max_concurrency from 16->6 for pool:serve-pool-rack7.

ajay.patel: on the network side I'm re-provisioning IB ports to move traffic off suspect link. Kicking off a fabric probe: `ibv_devinfo && rdma link probe` and raising ingress RX ring to see if queuing reduces drops.

sam.kim: started a targeted rolling restart of affected containers after drain to flush bad kvcache state. Observed immediate drop in CUDA OOM counts on two nodes after restart + batch tune.

environment-bot: Deploy job 4182 started: rollout (serve-config-batch-limits) -> pods: 24/24 updated.

jenna.hsu: customer comms: emailing impacted enterprise customers with ETA ~30m for stabilization. Notifying CSMs.

ajay.patel: fabric probe results: intermittent high TX latency spikes corresponding to rack-7 ToR NIC 0. Suspect NIC firmware flapping under microbursts. Scheduling NIC firmware bump and ToR reboot window, but that is disruptive.

derek: intermediate operational fix: enable regional fallback routing (route 10% of traffic away from rack-7 to us-west hot spare) and engage Dedicated fallback pools. I can flip the routing percentages now if approved.

maria.lee: approve. do the 10% shift. Keep autoscaling on so fallback can absorb.

derek: flipping traffic -> patched envoy weights: `envoyctl set-weight serve-route --from rack-7 0.9 --to us-west-hot 0.1`

sam.kim: monitoring: error rate down to 1.1% in last 3 mins, latency median back to normal but p95 still elevated for affected customers. CUDA OOMs drop to zero after restarts and batch reduction.

ajay.patel: network team will pursue NIC firmware and ToR linecard health check. For now we keep throttle and routing in place.

jenna.hsu: incident impact: partial degradation for ~12% of requests originating in us-east-rack7; 2 enterprise customers saw errors >5% during the window. No data loss.

maria.lee: creating incident timeline + action items. Handoff to Sam for monitoring/cleanup at 12:30Z. Sam, you're primary until remediation complete.

sam.kim: ack. I'll keep this thread live and update every 10m or on status change. Next check 12:20Z.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in place (routing shift, batch reduction, rolling restarts). Severity: P1 -> degraded (monitoring)."
